headline: Streaming and index-free search tools advance nucleotide and protein sequence alignment
label: Scalable Sequence Analysis Software
summary: Terabase-scale references and large search corpora demand alignment tools that avoid pre-indexing and scale to modern inputs.
synthesis: The three preprints share a focus on search and alignment engineering in which execution structure and input scale are treated as design constraints alongside accuracy. IndelFreeAligner is a streaming, indel-free aligner that avoids reference pre-indexing and is benchmarked against Bowtie1 and BLAST+ on terabase-scale references. Riboseek is a di-mer based RNA/DNA search and alignment tool reported to be more sensitive than BLASTN and nhmmer and 250-376x faster, with a web server. Reseek v3 applies parallel alignment over rich discrete structure alphabets with level-specific statistical models to protein structure search, and its title asserts the highest accuracy. The dominant thread is throughput and scalability, with the nucleotide tools distinguished by reported speed gains over established baselines, while Reseek's contribution is more centrally accuracy-oriented.
